claim_1.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from 43 RTS,S vaccine recipients on the day of the third vaccination (day 0), 24 h after the third vaccination (day 1), and 72 h after the third vaccination (day 3), using Significance Analysis of Microarrays, showed that genes associated with inflammatory responses, apoptosis, and the protein kinase cascade were up-regulated 24 h after the third vaccination (day 1) compared to the day of the third vaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: Figure 1 is a heat map showing the changes in expression of 63 genes associated with inflammatory responses on the day of the third vaccination and at 24 h and 72 h later. These genes are markedly up-regulated 24 h after vaccination; however, by 72 h after vaccination, they resolve to the levels of expression observed on the day of the third vaccination. Seventy-nine genes in the protein kinase cascade family and 107 genes in the apoptosis family follow the same pattern at 24 h and 72 h after the third vaccination.

Figure 1. Strong but transitory changes in genes associated with inflammatory processes are associated with vaccination with adjuvanted RTS,S. Heat map of genes associated with inflammatory responses in all vaccine recipients in the study on the day of the third vaccination and at 24 h and 72 h after vaccination. Sixty-three unique genes from inflammatory response pathways are significantly (false discovery rate [FDR], !1%) up-regulated 24 h after the third vaccination. Up-regulation of these genes resolves by 72 h after vaccination. Genes associated with apoptosis and the protein kinase cascade follow a similar pattern.

claim_3.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from 36 RTS,S vaccine recipients at baseline before vaccination and challenge, 39 vaccinated and challenged volunteers, and 12 challenged nonvaccinated volunteers, using principal component analysis of differentially expressed genes, showed distinct global expression patterns in vaccinated and challenged volunteers compared to challenged nonvaccinated volunteers.

sources.quote: We hypothesized that, regardless of protection status, the responses of the host to challenge would be different for individuals who were vaccinated and those who were vaccine naive.

Figure 2. The effect of vaccination and challenge on the global host response, as illustrated by principal components analysis of differentially expressed genes. Red spheres denote 36 RTS,S vaccine recipients at baseline before vaccination and challenge (group A). Blue spheres denote 39 volunteers who are vaccinated and then challenged (group B), and green spheres denote 12 control nonvaccinated volunteers who were challenged (group C). The separation of group A and group B reflects the combined effect of vaccination and challenge. The separation of group A and group C reflects the effects of challenge and challenge only. The separation of group B and group C indicates that volunteers who are vaccinated (group B) respond to challenge differently from those who are not vaccinated (group C).

claim_4.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from vaccine-naive persons challenged without vaccination and vaccinated persons challenged at day 5 after challenge, using principal component analysis of differentially expressed genes, showed a broader host response after challenge in vaccinated persons compared to challenged persons without vaccination.

sources.quote: The principal component analysis shown in Figure 2 shows 461 up-regulated genes and 626 down-regulated genes (identified at an FDR !1%) in persons challenged and infected without vaccination. Challenge after vaccination results in up-regulation of 6219 genes and down-regulation of 5670 genes, suggesting an extensive and broader host response associated with vaccination.

Figure 2. The effect of vaccination and challenge on the global host response, as illustrated by principal components analysis of differentially expressed genes. Red spheres denote 36 RTS,S vaccine recipients at baseline before vaccination and challenge (group A). Blue spheres denote 39 volunteers who are vaccinated and then challenged (group B), and green spheres denote 12 control nonvaccinated volunteers who were challenged (group C). The separation of group A and group B reflects the combined effect of vaccination and challenge. The separation of group A and group C reflects the effects of challenge and challenge only. The separation of group B and group C indicates that volunteers who are vaccinated (group B) respond to challenge differently from those who are not vaccinated (group C).

claim_5.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from 39 vaccine recipients at day 5 after challenge, using prediction analysis of microarrays with R, showed that a 393-gene classifier sorted samples into protected, delayed-onset, and nonprotected outcome groups with 100% accuracy.

sources.quote: PAM-R was used to identify sets of classifier genes capable of sorting samples (n p 39 subjects) into protected, not protected, and delayed onset of disease categories, on day 5 after challenge. Figure 3A shows the results of PAM-R for these groups.

Figure 3. Prediction analysis of microarrays with R (PAM-R) classification analysis of outcome at 5 days after challenge. A, PAM-R analysis with 100% accuracy in classification by the 393 genes in the classifier set. Patients 1–13 belong to the protected group, patients 14–24 belong to the group with delayed onset of disease, and patients 25–39 belong to the nonprotected group.

claim_6.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from 39 vaccine recipients at day 5 after challenge, using prediction analysis of microarrays with R and DAVID annotation, showed that genes associated with progression through the cell cycle and regulation of apoptosis/programmed cell death predominated in the 393-gene classifier set compared to other annotated functional categories.

sources.quote: Genes in the classifier set are those that can be annotated by DAVID and for which P ! .05. Those associated with both positive and negative regulation of progression through the cell cycle and with control of apoptosis and programmed cell death are predominant.

Figure 3. Prediction analysis of microarrays with R (PAM-R) classification analysis of outcome at 5 days after challenge. C, A pie chart of those functional categories in the classifier that are annotated by DAVID at biological process level 5. Genes associated with progression through the cell cycle and the regulation of apoptosis are predominant. Only categories for which P ! .05 are shown.

claim_7.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from 37 vaccine recipients 2 weeks after the third vaccination (day 14) and before challenge, using gene set enrichment analysis, showed that genes in the proteasome degradation pathway were up-regulated in protected persons compared to nonprotected persons.

sources.quote: Figure 4A shows the enrichment of genes in the proteasome degradation pathway that are up-regulated in persons in the protected group. Vertical black bars denote the 32 genes in the proteasome degradation pathway. Bars are concentrated toward the right side of the graph, indicating that their expression is up-regulated in the protected group.

Figure 4. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) identification of genes in the immunoproteasome pathway associated with the processing of major histocompatibility complex class 1 peptides and differentially up-regulated in persons protected by RTS,S vaccination A, Running enrichment score (RES) showing that the proteasome degradation pathway is up-regulated in the protected group.

claim_8.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from 37 vaccine recipients 2 weeks after the third vaccination (day 14) and before challenge, using gene set enrichment analysis, showed that the proteasome degradation pathway was the only gene set with both a significant P value and a multiple-test-corrected false discovery rate below the default cutoff compared to other tested gene sets.

sources.quote: Figure 4B shows the gene set null distribution analysis, which indicates that the genes in the proteasome degradation pathway are statistically significant at P ! .001, with an FDR of 0.086. This was the only set of genes with both a significant P value and a multiple test correction FDR that was less than the default value of 0.25.

Figure 4. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) identification of genes in the immunoproteasome pathway associated with the processing of major histocompatibility complex class 1 peptides and differentially up-regulated in persons protected by RTS,S vaccination B, Permutation test of the significance of the proteasome degradation pathway. The GSEA algorithm executes a permutation test to calculate the nominal P value and false discovery rate (FDR) of identified pathways. After multiple test correction, the FDR of the proteasome degradation pathway is 0.086, which is less than the default cutoff of 0.25.

claim_9.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from protected and nonprotected vaccine recipients 2 weeks after the third vaccination (day 14) and before challenge, using gene set enrichment analysis, showed that core enrichment genes in the proteasome degradation pathway were differentially up-regulated in protected persons compared to nonprotected persons.

sources.quote: Figure 4C presents a heat map showing differential regulation of genes in the proteasome degradation pathway in the nonprotected and protected groups.

Figure 4. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) identification of genes in the immunoproteasome pathway associated with the processing of major histocompatibility complex class 1 peptides and differentially up-regulated in persons protected by RTS,S vaccination C, A heat map showing the up-regulation of core enrichment genes in the immunoproteasome pathway in the protected groups.

claim_10.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from protected and nonprotected vaccine recipients 2 weeks after the third vaccination (day 14) and before challenge, using gene set enrichment analysis, showed that up-regulation of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 in protected persons indicated involvement of the immunoproteasome pathway responsible for processing antigenic peptides compared to nonprotected persons.

sources.quote: Up-regulation of PSME2 (a component of the 11S regulator), PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9, as revealed by this analysis, indicates that the specific pathway responsible for differential response to the vaccine impinges on the processing of antigenic peptides.

Figure 5. The functional pathway of the genes in the immunoproteasome pathway identified by gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), as up-regulated in persons protected by vaccination with RTS,S. The specific up-regulation of PSME2 (a component of the 11S regulator) in persons protected by the vaccine directs the formation of the immunoproteasome associated with major histocompatibility complex class 1 processing rather than that of the constitutive proteasome associated with general protein degradation.

claim_11.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from vaccine recipients at study entry and 2 weeks after the third vaccination (day 14), using gene set enrichment analysis, showed no up-regulation of the proteasome degradation pathway in the protected group before vaccination compared to the protected group after vaccination.

sources.quote: To show the specificity of these observations to the vaccine, gene expression results from subjects at study entry were subjected to GSEA. No gene sets reached an FDR of !0.25, indicating that the proteasome degradation pathway was not up-regulated in the protected group before vaccination.

claim_12.claim: RT-PCR analysis of PBMCs from 3 randomly chosen protected and nonprotected persons 2 weeks after the third vaccination (day 14) showed that PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 were up-regulated in protected individuals compared to nonprotected individuals.

sources.quote: Figure 6A shows reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction confirmation of differential gene expression in 3 randomly chosen samples obtained from protected and not protected outcome groups at 2 weeks after the third vaccination and identified by expression data as genes associated with regulation of MHC processing in the immunoproteasome pathway.

Figure 6. Reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) confirmation of the up-regulation of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 in protected individuals. A, The fold change in gene expression (as shown on the y-axis) relative to the samples with the lowest expression value for a given gene and assay. Four genes (PSME2, PSMB9, PSMB6, and PSMA4) are displayed along the x-axis. Triangles and stars denote samples obtained from protected and nonprotected individuals, respectively. Fold change values denoted by triangles are consistently greater than those denoted by stars, confirming the up-regulation of these genes in protected individuals.

claim_13.claim: RT-PCR analysis of PBMCs from 3 randomly chosen protected and nonprotected persons 2 weeks after the third vaccination (day 14) showed that RT-PCR-based fold changes were positively associated with Affymetrix GeneChip-based fold changes for PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9.

sources.quote: The correlation coefficient for concordance of these 2 independent techniques was r p 0.886, as shown in Figure 6B.

Figure 6. Reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) confirmation of the up-regulation of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 in protected individuals. B, The fold change in gene expression (as shown on the x-axis) detected by RT-PCR and the fold change (as shown on the y-axis) detected by Affymetrix GeneChip technology. The correlation coefficient is 0.886.
